expectr: pipeline checkpoints for data expectations

Source: R/expectr-package.R
expectr-package.Rd

Statistical production code lives or dies on small assumptions: no duplicate units, no negative amounts, no person with two addresses at once. expectr states each assumption as one line in the pipeline, a checkpoint, built on a single idea: express the rule as "the set of violations must be empty", build that set with ordinary dplyr, and pass it on. See vignette("expectr").

Details

Where to start

  • expect_empty(): the violation set you pipe in has no rows.

  • expect_none(): no row matches a condition; returns the full data.

  • expect_unique(), expect_balanced(), expect_no_overlap(): the register rules that are awkward to write as a filter().

  • tally_violations(): counts violations for many rules at once, and leaves the verdict to you.

  • flag_duplicates() and view_types(): inspect duplicates and column types before you settle on a rule.

Why a package of its own

The checkpoints started in the daos package. They moved here because they share an engine and a contract the rest of daos does not: every function either judges a violation set or helps build one, with the same messages, logging, dumps and condition class, and the same grouping engine for keys such as cpr. daos re-exports them for existing scripts.
